external_sources.title: Towards a standard for pointing device evaluation, perspectives on 27 years of Fitts' law research in HCI
external_sources.locator: Int. J. Human-Computer Studies 61, pp. 751-756 (abstract, sections 1-2, recommendations I-IV, footnotes 2, 3, 7, 11)
claims_supported: Fitts' law describes the relationship between movement time, distance and accuracy for people engaged in rapid aimed movements (p. 751).
It applies to pointing and dragging with mouse, trackball, stylus, joystick and touchscreen (p. 752).
Speed and accuracy trade off; both should be reported separately (p. 752, fn 3).
Movement time excludes homing, dwell and reaction time (p. 755, fn 7).
The model is bounded to rapid aimed movement; leisurely movements are outside this use (p. 756, fn 11).
Shannon formulation ID = log2(D/W + 1); effective width We = 4.133 sigma adjusts for accuracy (pp. 755-756).
Angle of movement confounds results; ISO 9241-9 uses a circular multidirectional task (p. 753).
external_sources.limitations: Laboratory pointing paradigm; the paper is about modelling and device comparison, not about visual search, decision time, label comprehension or whole-task UI design.
external_sources.reuse_status: cite_and_paraphrase; no text copied beyond short quotes

external_sources.title: The information capacity of the human motor system in controlling the amplitude of movement
external_sources.access_extent: bibliographic_only; University of Iowa PDF returned HTTP 404 and PsycNet page did not render. Task details are taken from X01's description of the Fitts paradigm (Fig. 1, serial and discrete tasks), not from the original.
claims_supported: Bibliographic identity of the original model paper.
external_sources.limitations: Original experimental tasks, apparatus and participants were not inspected this session. Do not quote Fitts (1954) directly from this packet.

external_sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
external_sources.access_extent: summarizer. 2.5.8 text from this pass was garbled and is superseded by X04. Other criterion texts matched known wording but were not visually confirmed.
claims_supported: 3.3.4 (AA): for legal commitments, financial transactions, modification/deletion of user-controllable data, or test responses, at least one of Reversible, Checked or Confirmed.
2.5.7 (AA): dragging functionality has a single-pointer non-drag alternative unless essential.
2.5.5 (AAA): targets at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels (with exceptions).
3.3.7 (A) Redundant Entry; 2.2.5 (AAA) continue without data loss after re-authentication; 2.2.6 (AAA) warn of inactivity timeouts that could lose data unless data preserved >20 hours.
1.4.1 (A) color not the only visual means; 4.1.3 (AA) status messages programmatically determinable without focus; 2.4.11 (AA) focused component not entirely hidden by author content.
external_sources.limitations: Conformance requires a real accessibility evaluation; a design review cannot claim it. Criteria define minimums, not optimal design.
external_sources.reuse_status: cite; W3C documents may be quoted with attribution

external_sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 2.5.8: Target Size (Minimum)
external_sources.locator: Success Criterion text box; Intent section
external_sources.access_extent: Official W3C Understanding page read by Codex; criterion text, five exceptions and intent checked. The Understanding page is informative; normative criterion is X03.
claims_supported: Target at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels except Spacing, Equivalent, Inline, User Agent Control, Essential.
Intent: this is a minimum; larger targets help many people; for important controls consider 2.5.5 Enhanced.
external_sources.limitations: Informative explanation rather than the normative criterion itself; pointer targets only; does not settle thumb reach or a specific audience.

external_sources.title: The Magical Mystery Four: How is Working Memory Capacity Limited, and Why?
external_sources.locator: Current Directions in Psychological Science 19(1); main text sections on capacity and boundary conditions
external_sources.access_extent: summarizer over PMC full text; short phrases summarizer-reported, not visually confirmed
claims_supported: A central store limited to roughly 3 to 5 meaningful chunks in young adults (summarizer-reported phrase).
The limit is observed when rehearsal and grouping are prevented or controlled; it concerns information held in mind, not information that remains available in the environment.
external_sources.limitations: Does not establish limits on the number of options visible on a screen, navigation items or buttons. Population is mainly young adults in lab tasks.

external_sources.title: NASA-Task Load Index (NASA-TLX); 20 Years Later
external_sources.locator: Proceedings of the HFES 50th Annual Meeting; pp. 1-3 of the PDF (Background, Focus, Methodological Issues)
claims_supported: Workload represents human cost in meeting task demands (Background).
Six subscales: Mental, Physical and Temporal Demands, Frustration, Effort, Performance (Background).
TLX ratings need not track performance; an apparently undemanding vigilance task may still carry high workload through boredom (p. 3).
Adding, deleting or redefining subscales requires re-establishing validity, sensitivity and reliability (p. 3).
Raw TLX (unweighted) was more, less or equally sensitive across 29 comparisons (p. 3).
external_sources.limitations: Subjective self-report; collected from actual operators during or after a task. An AI reviewer cannot produce a TLX score by inspecting a screen.
external_sources.reuse_status: cite; do not reproduce the rating form

external_sources.title: Memory for goals: an activation-based model
external_sources.institution: Michigan State University; Naval Research Laboratory
claims_supported: A suspended goal can only be retrieved with help from priming from an associated cue (p. 40).
The cue must be available both when the goal is suspended (to create the link) and when it is resumed (p. 40).
Resuming at the right step without redundant or skipped steps can matter greatly in domains like aviation (p. 40).
external_sources.limitations: Model fitted to Tower of Hanoi data; interface transfer (resumption cues in software) is this packet's inference, not the paper's tested result.

external_sources.title: Emotional Expressions Reconsidered: Challenges to Inferring Emotion From Human Facial Movements
external_sources.locator: Psychological Science in the Public Interest 20(1), 1-68; APS summary page
external_sources.access_extent: Publisher summary page inspected by Codex and earlier via summarizer; full 68-page text not read.
claims_supported: The publisher summary rejects a universal direct mapping from facial movements to specific emotions.
The reviewed evidence does not support reliability, specificity, generalizability and validity for a direct mapping from facial configurations to emotions.
external_sources.limitations: About facial movements specifically; does not say emotion is unimportant or unmeasurable by self-report, context or behavior.

external_sources.title: Question and Questionnaire Design (Chapter 9, Handbook of Survey Research, 2nd ed.)
external_sources.locator: pp. 263-265 (chapter overview, 9.1 Conventional Wisdom, 9.1.1 Optimizing versus Satisficing)
claims_supported: Eight conventional-wisdom wording recommendations, including avoiding leading or loaded questions and asking about one thing at a time (p. 264).
Question-order advice, including filter questions so respondents are not asked irrelevant items (p. 264).
Satisficing: fatigued or unmotivated respondents shortcut comprehension, retrieval, judgment and response (p. 265).
The chapter separately reviews acquiescence response bias and methods for avoiding it (p. 263).
external_sources.limitations: The p. 264 list is labelled 'conventional wisdom', which the authors distinguish from the methodological research reviewed later; the later sections were not read.
external_sources.reuse_status: cite_and_paraphrase; Emerald copyright, all rights reserved

external_sources.title: Crossing the Bridge over Norman's Gulf of Execution: Revealing Feedforward's True Identity
external_sources.institution: Hasselt University; University of Technology Sydney; Eindhoven University of Technology
external_sources.locator: PDF pp. 1-4: Introduction, Fig. 1, Background, Feedforward Definitions, Fig. 5
claims_supported: Feedforward tells users what the result of their action will be, before the action (Introduction; quoting Djajadiningrat et al.).
Feedback bridges the Gulf of Evaluation after action; feedforward bridges the Gulf of Execution before action (Background, Fig. 1).
Perceived affordances invite a particular action but do not communicate its purpose (Background).
Wensveen's inherent, augmented and functional feedforward classes (Fig. 5).
external_sources.limitations: Conceptual framework with examples, not an effect-size study.

external_sources.title: Representations in Distributed Cognitive Tasks
external_sources.institution: The Ohio State University; Apple Computer
external_sources.locator: Cognitive Science 18, pp. 87-88 (abstract; The Representational Effect)
claims_supported: Many tasks require processing information distributed across the internal mind and the external environment (abstract).
Representational effect: isomorphic representations of the same formal structure can cause dramatically different cognitive behavior (p. 88).
external_sources.limitations: Puzzle isomorphs (Tower of Hanoi); transfer to dashboards is this packet's design inference.

external_sources.title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
claims_supported: Heuristics are broad rules of thumb rather than specific usability rules.
Developed with Rolf Molich in 1990 and refined by Nielsen in 1994.
#3 addresses an exit; #6 advises making relevant elements, actions and options visible to reduce recall.
external_sources.limitations: Practitioner heuristics; finding a heuristic violation is a hypothesis about user difficulty, not evidence of it.

external_sources.title: Open-Loop Response of Control System for Stability Margin Analysis
external_sources.access_extent: Official page independently read by Codex lead; user coursework MATLAB video not accessible.
claims_supported: For the documented control analysis, open-loop response combines the plant and controller and excludes feedback.
external_sources.limitations: Supports engineering terminology only. Applying open-loop to user-interface feedback is an analogy proposed by this packet, not a MathWorks UI recommendation.
